candidates.title: Pituitary Stalk Interruption Syndrome in Adulthood: Diagnostic Recognition, Clinical Spectrum, and Long-Term Follow-Up.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome is usually diagnosed during childhood, and data on outcomes in adulthood are limited. This retrospective, single-center study evaluated the diagnostic history, endocrine phenotype, and clinical outcomes of 14 adults with radiologically confirmed pituitary stalk interruption syndrome. The cohort comprised eight men and six women, with a mean age of 28.8±6.4 years and a mean documented follow-up at our center of 5.6±3.2 years. Hypopituitarism was diagnosed during childhood in 12 patients and during adulthood in 2 patients. Thirteen patients had deficiencies of all four anterior pituitary hormone axes, whereas one patient had growth hormone and gonadotropic deficiencies with preserved corticotropic and thyrotropic functions. In six patients diagnosed during childhood, pituitary stalk interruption syndrome was recognized only after later reassessment of pituitary imaging. Eleven patients received growth hormone treatment during childhood, and 13 of 14 patients reached their calculated target height. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and dyslipidemia were each present in 10 patients. Four patients had bone mineral density below the expected range for age. One female patient achieved a live birth following in vitro fertilization. In this real-world cohort, the skeletal and metabolic findings observed despite generally favorable growth outcomes support the need for lifelong endocrine follow-up.

candidates.title: Visual and Anatomical Outcomes of Intravitreal Ranibizumab Combined with Focal/Grid Macular Laser for Center-Involved Diabetic Macular Edema: A Real-World Retrospective Cohort Study.
candidates.abstract: Center-involved diabetic macular edema (CI-DME) is a major cause of vision loss in non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. Anti-VEGF therapy is standard, but adjunctive focal/grid macular laser may reduce treatment burden in selected eyes. This study evaluated ranibizumab combined with individualized focal/grid laser in Chinese patients with CI-DME. In this retrospective propensity-matched cohort study, 196 eyes with NPDR-related CI-DME received ranibizumab plus focal/grid macular laser (n = 98) or focal/grid laser alone (n = 98) and were followed for 6 months. Baseline OCT and fluorescein angiography were reviewed to characterize DME morphology. The primary outcome was change in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA); secondary outcomes included central macular thickness (CMT), ≥0.2 LogMAR gain, injection frequency, and adverse events. At month 6, BCVA improved more in the combination group than in controls (-0.17 ± 0.12 vs. -0.10 ± 0.09 LogMAR; p = 0.002). A ≥ 0.2 LogMAR gain occurred in 57.6% versus 31.8% of eyes (p = 0.001). CMT reduction was also greater with combination therapy (152.3 ± 71.5 μm vs. 86.7 ± 68.2 μm; p < 0.001), and ≥20% CMT reduction occurred in 65.2% versus 38.4% of eyes. Nearly half of combination-treated eyes required no additional injections beyond the initial three. Adverse events were rare and similar. Ranibizumab combined with individualized focal/grid macular laser improved visual and anatomical outcomes, reduced injection burden, and showed acceptable safety in selected CI-DME eyes.

candidates.title: Aesthetic Improvement of Glabellar Lines with Liquid RelabotulinumtoxinA Treatment in a 12-Month Randomized Controlled Study.
candidates.abstract: RelabotulinumtoxinA (relaBoNT-A) is a novel, complex-free, ready-to-use liquid BoNT-A for aesthetic use. This double-blind, Phase 3b study evaluated long-term (12-month) efficacy, satisfaction, safety, and time to onset of effect of relaBoNT-A for glabellar lines (GLs). Subjects were randomized 3:1 to a single dose of 50 U relaBoNT-A or placebo. RelaBoNT-A was superior to placebo at Month 1 based on subject-reported Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale (GAIS) responder rates at maximum frown (primary endpoint), 92.9% (92/99 subjects) versus 9.1% (3/33 subjects), p<0.001. GAIS response after relaBoNT-A treatment remained high through Months 9 (42.7%) and 12 (37.8%), as did investigator-assessed GL severity (GL-ILA) ≥1-grade improvement at maximum frown at Months 6 (57.4%), 9 (28.1%), and 12 (12.2%). GAIS and GL-ILA showed onset of effect in 39.8% and 43.9% of relaBoNT-A-treated subjects within 1 day. Investigators reported increased confidence in dosing consistency with the ready-to-use product at baseline (98.0% relaBoNT-A vs. 100% placebo), and that they could achieve consistent (99.0% vs. 64.5%) and natural-looking results (98.0% vs. 64.5%) at Month 1. Subject satisfaction was higher for relaBoNT-A than placebo from Day 1 through Month 12. Two-thirds of subjects preferred treatment with relaBoNT-A to prior treatments with powder BoNT-As. Treatment-related adverse events (all mild) occurred in 8.1% of subjects. RelaBoNT-A showed rapid onset of effect from Day 1, with duration of effect through Month 6 for most subjects, and beyond 6 months for some. Injectors were highly satisfied with product usability, and subjects remained satisfied through Month 12. Treatment was well tolerated.

candidates.title: Compassion-Focused Implementation of Smartwatches in Acute Mental Health Care: Mixed Method Replicated Single-Case Study.
candidates.abstract: Smartwatches can support mental health care by providing insights into activity and sleep, which are closely linked to mental health and daily functioning. However, their implementation in mental health care practice remains limited. Professionals can feel resistance toward digital mental health interventions if they feel their use is not aligned with therapeutic values, and report a need for guidance on how to use technologies in ways that do align with such values. Compassion, a core value in mental health care, may offer a meaningful frame for implementation. Therefore, we previously co-designed compassion-focused implementation materials: a card set offering practical suggestions of how smartwatch data can support group treatments in ways that counter the self-optimization logic of commercial devices and instead align with compassion. The current study evaluated the compassion-focused card set in practice, to explore whether the introduction of the card set influenced the use of smartwatches in treatment sessions, and mental health professionals' experienced compassion when working with smartwatches, the therapeutic alliance, and acceptance of smartwatches. The card set was evaluated in a mixed methods replicated single-case design with 5 social psychiatric nurses from an acute mental health care team. Data collection included pre- and post-questionnaires, repeated measures, a focus group, and interviews. For smartwatch use, no significant intervention effects were found, though several participants did report the start or increase of use of the smartwatch in sessions during the intervention phase. For compassion, only P2 showed a significant effect of the intervention on experienced compassion when using smartwatches (Tau-U=0.53, 95% CI -0.11 to 0.86; P=.02). This participant reported that the card set helped to make the use of smartwatches more concrete and insightful. For therapeutic alliance and acceptance of the smartwatches, no intervention effects were found. These scores were rather stable over time for most participants. The card set was experienced as flexible and easy to use, supporting session structure and enabling more in-depth, compassionate conversations. At the same time, barriers to sustained smartwatch integration included low patient uptake, challenges in mixed groups in which only some patients wore the smartwatch, and varying digital affinity among professionals. These findings suggest that compassion-focused materials may trigger initial adoption and help reframe smartwatch use in line with therapeutic values. Broader implementation strategies, including further training and tailoring to patient readiness, are required for sustainable integration.

candidates.title: Innovation and challenges of spoken and aphasic speech data: Introducing the CACLA corpora.
candidates.abstract: Aphasia assessment in Modern Greek is hampered by the scarcity of authentic spoken data, annotated resources, and adaptive clinical instruments; SUBTLEX-GR offers frequency counts drawn from translated subtitles, yet clinicians still lack the psycholinguistic norms routinely available for English and other major languages. Computational linguistics provides a bridge between linguistic theory and clinical practice by allowing theoretical assumptions to be tested through computational implementation, and we exploit this bridge to address the gap. We present the CACLA (Clinical Application of Computational Linguistics for Aphasia) corpora, comprising: (a) GRTVScripts (Greek television scripts), (b) GRNewsTexts (broadcast news files), (c) ENGTVGreekSubtitles (Greek subtitles), and (d) AphasiaSpeech (clinical naming and narration data from speakers with aphasia). Using established corpus tools (AntConc, Voyant, Sketch Engine, GPT-4), we derive word frequencies, contextual diversity, Part-of-Speech-specific frequencies, and bigram measures, yielding the comprehensive Modern Greek norms that clinical assessment has so far lacked. These resources directly underpin the development of a computer-adaptive anomia test for Greek, addressing the limitations of current instruments and grounding item selection in both cognitive and psychometric theory. The result is a tangible step towards theoretically grounded, data-driven aphasia evaluation tailored to Greek-speaking patients.

candidates.title: Acute Sheehan Syndrome Presenting as Panhypopituitarism and Reversible Cardiac Dysfunction in a Patient With Sickle Cell Disease: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Sheehan syndrome is an uncommon cause of hypopituitarism resulting from ischemic pituitary necrosis following severe postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) and hypotension. Its presentation can be delayed and non-specific, and it is rarely reported in the context of mild PPH with severe hemolysis. Here, we describe a 31-year-old woman with underlying sickle cell disease (SCD) who developed panhypopituitarism and reversible cardiac dysfunction after an 11-week period of progressive symptoms following spontaneous vaginal delivery complicated by an estimated blood loss of 700 mL and severe hemolysis. Pituitary hormonal replacement therapy, together with heart failure treatment, resulted in marked clinical and biochemical improvement, with normalization of metabolic abnormalities and recovery of cardiac function. This case suggests a possible association between Sheehan syndrome and postpartum blood loss of 700 mL accompanied by severe hemolysis, though this remains hypothetical based on a single case.

candidates.title: Solitary Neurofibroma in the Submental Region of a 15-Year-Old Adolescent: A Case Report and Review of Literature.
candidates.abstract: Neurofibroma is a benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor composed of Schwann cells and fibroblasts. It may occur sporadically or as part of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). Solitary neurofibroma arising in the submental region of an adolescent is extremely rare. We report a case of a solitary submental neurofibroma in a 15-year-old male and highlight its diagnostic and management implications. A 15-year-old adolescent boy presented with a chronic, painless right submental swelling that had been present for one year and had enlarged over the preceding three months. Clinical examination revealed a rubbery, nontender, approximately 3×3×4 cm mass without skin changes or systemic symptoms. There was no personal or family history suggestive of NF1, neural tumors, or pheochromocytoma. Ultrasound and CT imaging showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass consistent with a benign neurogenic tumor. The mass was completely excised via a submental incision. Histopathological examination confirmed a solitary neurofibroma with Schwann cell and fibroblast proliferation within a collagen matrix, Antoni A and B patterns, and positive S-100 immunostaining, with no evidence of malignancy. The postoperative course was uneventful, and tongue and floor-of-mouth function were preserved. Solitary submental neurofibroma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of submental masses in adolescents, even in the absence of NF1 features. Complete surgical excision is the treatment of choice and allows definitive histopathological diagnosis. A thorough evaluation for NF1 is recommended to guide long-term management and follow-up.

candidates.title: Minimal Clinically Important Differences of Common Anxiety Scales in Older Adults with Parkinson's Disease with Anxiety Following Cognitive Behavioral Therapy.
candidates.abstract: To establish minimal clinically important difference (MCID) thresholds for the Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale-Anxiety Subscale (HADS-A), Parkinson's Anxiety Scale (PAS), and Geriatric Anxiety Inventory (GAI) in older adults with Parkinson's disease and anxiety (PD-A), and identify optimal thresholds for classifying clinical improvement. This cohort study included 110 older adults with PD-A who completed individualized Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy (CBT). Anxiety was assessed before and after intervention using the four scales. Clinical change was anchored to the Global Rating of Change (GRoC) scale. MCIDs were estimated using anchor- and distribution-based methods. Anchor-based between-group mean-change estimates yielded MCIDs of -2.38 (BAI), -3.64 (HADS-A), -3.13 (PAS), and -2.95 (GAI). Receiver operating characteristic analysis using the Youden index identified complementary classification cut-offs of ≤ -2 for the BAI, HADS-A, and PAS, and ≤ -1 for the GAI. This study provides MCID thresholds for four anxiety measures in older adults with PD-A, offering clinically relevant benchmarks for interpreting treatment-related changes and evaluating improvement. Clinicians can use the estimated MCID thresholds to interpret whether changes in anxiety scores following CBT are likely to represent clinically meaningful improvement in older adults with PD-A. The complementary ROC-derived cutoffs may assist in identifying individual improvement, while combined use of anxiety measures, particularly the PAS and HADS-A, may enhance sensitivity to clinically meaningful change.

candidates.title: Durable Complete Response to Pembrolizumab for Postoperative Nodal Recurrence of Lynch Syndrome-Associated Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Germline mutations in mismatch repair genes cause Lynch syndrome and are associated with upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). Tumors with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) may respond favorably to immune checkpoint inhibitors. A 54-year-old woman with Lynch syndrome and a germline MSH2 mutation developed right renal pelvic carcinoma. The tumor was diagnosed as a pT3 high-grade urothelial carcinoma, and the patient underwent laparoscopic nephroureterectomy. She was subsequently administered adjuvant gemcitabine and carboplatin due to a contraindication for cisplatin. Due to nodal recurrence, pembrolizumab was initiated at 200 mg every 3 weeks, achieving a complete radiological and metabolic response after five cycles. The course was complicated by immune-related adrenal insufficiency, which was managed with corticosteroid replacement therapy. Pembrolizumab may achieve a durable complete response in Lynch syndrome-associated UTUC. MSI screening should be considered in UTUC to guide decision-making.

candidates.title: Scleroderma-Like Phenotype in a Patient With Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis and Acromegaly: A Triple Diagnostic Challenge.
candidates.abstract: Systemic sclerosis, transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis, and acromegaly are rare disorders that share several clinical manifestations, including skin thickening, heart failure, dysphagia, fatigue, and soft tissue enlargement. Their coexistence is exceptionally rare and poses a significant diagnostic challenge, increasing the risk of premature diagnostic closure. We report a 78-year-old man who developed progressive diffuse skin thickening following spinal cord stimulator revision. Positive RNA polymerase III antibodies supported a diagnosis of diffuse systemic sclerosis. Evaluation of worsening edema and exertional dyspnea revealed severe concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with relative apical sparing on echocardiography, and technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy confirmed transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. Persistent macroglossia, coarse facial features, prior carpal tunnel syndrome, and a remote history of increasing ring and shoe size prompted endocrine evaluation, which demonstrated elevated insulin-like growth factor-1 levels, failure of growth hormone suppression, and a pituitary macroadenoma consistent with acromegaly. The patient underwent successful transsphenoidal resection with biochemical remission. This case highlights the importance of reconsidering the differential diagnosis when clinical features are not fully explained by an established diagnosis. Recognizing atypical and discordant findings prevented premature diagnostic closure and led to the identification of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis and acromegaly in a patient with a rapidly progressive scleroderma-like phenotype.

candidates.title: Beware of Tall Stature: Growth Hormone Excess Associated with a Rare Parasellar Extra-Axial Tumour-Diagnostic and Management Challenges in a Resource-Limited Setting.
candidates.abstract: Tall stature can be the sole indicator of growth hormone (GH) excess, which causes pituitary gigantism before epiphyseal fusion. In developing regions like Indonesia, a lack of systematic screening often delays diagnosis. While classic presentations involve accelerated linear growth, atypical cases may be dominated by neurological signs, such as seizures secondary to tumour mass effect. A 14-year-old boy presented with a 2-year history of rapidly accelerating growth velocity, increasing shoe size, and a 6-month history of severe morning headaches accompanied by drug-resistant focal seizures. Endocrine evaluations revealed significantly elevated basal GH (4.27 ng/ml) and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) levels (536 ng/ml). Brain magnetic resonance imaging identified a large parasellar extra-axial tumour with suprasellar extension. The patient underwent a craniotomy and tumour excision; histopathology subsequently confirmed a rare, aggressive malignant mesenchymal tumour. Postoperatively, the patient achieved seizure resolution and normalization of GH and IGF-1 levels. However, he developed evolving pituitary dysfunction consistent with multiple pituitary hormone deficiency (MPHD), specifically central hypothyroidism, necessitating targeted hormonal replacement therapy and continuous clinical follow-up. GH excess and gigantism can arise secondary to parasellar pathology rather than intrinsic pituitary disease, with neurological features like refractory epilepsy occasionally preceding classic endocrine manifestations. Rapid adolescent growth paired with neurological signs warrants urgent structural neuroimaging. Meticulous perioperative pituitary monitoring and early multidisciplinary involvement are essential to optimize long-term patient outcomes. Pituitary gigantism can be driven by extra-axial parasellar masses rather than intrinsic pituitary adenomas, operating via mass-effect compression that disrupts hypothalamic somatostatin inhibition.Drug-resistant epilepsy and severe headaches caused by local tumour infiltration can dominate the clinical picture, meaning rapid adolescent growth paired with neurological symptoms mandates urgent magnetic resonance imaging of the brain.Postoperative multiple pituitary hormone deficiency often evolves silently over weeks or months, requiring lifelong, multidisciplinary surveillance to detect late-stage deficiencies like secondary adrenal insufficiency.

candidates.title: Adrenal ganglioneuroma in an adolescent presenting as an incidentaloma: Imaging-pathology correlation and diagnostic challenges: A case report.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal ganglioneuroma (AGN) is a rare, benign, and usually nonfunctioning tumor arising from neural crest-derived sympathetic ganglion cells. Preoperative diagnosis is difficult because the clinical presentation is often nonspecific, and imaging findings overlap with those of other adrenal neoplasms. We describe an adolescent adrenal incidentaloma with detailed imaging-pathology correlation, adding to the small number of reported adolescent cases. A previously healthy 16-year-old male underwent contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) after a bicycle accident. No traumatic injury was identified, but imaging incidentally revealed a well-circumscribed right adrenal mass measuring approximately 6.1 cm × 3.6 cm × 5.0 cm. CT and magnetic resonance imaging showed progressive, persistent enhancement across the arterial, venous, and delayed phases without demonstrable washout (attenuation increased from 20 Hounsfield units unenhanced to 55 Hounsfield units in the venous phase, with further qualitative enhancement on 15-minute delayed images) and no intralesional fat, suggesting a non-adenomatous lesion and raising suspicion for a neurogenic tumor. Biochemical evaluation showed no evidence of hormonal hypersecretion. Histopathological examination after resection established the diagnosis of AGN. The patient underwent right adrenalectomy because of the size and radiologically indeterminate nature of the mass. The postoperative course was uneventful. Transient elevation of blood pressure noted during follow-up prompted biochemical reevaluation, which showed no evidence of excess catecholamine. Follow-up CT at 9 months showed no recurrence. Progressive delayed enhancement without washout and absence of signal loss on opposed-phase magnetic resonance imaging, a pattern previously described in ganglioneuroma, may suggest the diagnosis preoperatively, although definitive diagnosis requires histopathological confirmation. Complete surgical excision established the diagnosis and achieved a favorable short-term outcome; the excellent long-term prognosis of AGN is supported by the published literature, and our patient remains recurrence-free at 9 months.

candidates.title: A Diagnostic Conundrum: A Hemorrhagic Adrenal Mass With Discordant Radiological, Biochemical, and Pathologic Features.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal incidentalomas vary in their identity, making accurate diagnosis essential for management. Interpretation of these lesions using radiology, biochemistry, or pathology can be confounded by hemorrhagic changes, medication effects, and limitations of imaging. To prevent misclassification, an integrated assessment is crucial. We present a case of a 71-year-old male with an incidentally discovered left adrenal mass that exhibited computed tomography and MRI imaging findings concerning for pheochromocytoma or adrenal malignancy. Biochemical analysis ruled out pheochromocytoma and was suggestive of possible glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid co-secretion, although clinical urgency of surgical resection precluded completion of confirmatory endocrinologic testing. The lesion was initially diagnosed as a benign endothelial adrenal cyst on pathologic review. Because of the discordance among the radiological, biochemical, and initial pathologic findings, an integrated histologic re-evaluation was requested. The mass was ultimately reclassified as an adrenocortical adenoma with extensive hemorrhagic and cystic changes. This case highlights the importance of multidisciplinary integration when evaluating adrenal lesions with confounding features and underscores how suggestive (though incomplete) biochemical evidence can appropriately drive pathological re-evaluation.

candidates.title: Non-diabetic endocrine neuropathies: A practical approach to diagnosis and clinical evaluation.
candidates.abstract: Peripheral neuropathy has diverse etiologies, with endocrine disorders beyond diabetes representing significant, yet frequently underrecognized causes. While diabetic neuropathy is well established, this article specifically excludes a detailed discussion of diabetic neuropathy to focus on less-recognized endocrine causes and presents a practical diagnostic algorithm for their earlier and more accurate identification. A focused narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus and ScienceDirect (2015-2025). From 2,318 screened records, 154 studies were included after full-text review of 298 articles. Evidence was synthesized by etiology, mechanism, clinical presentation and diagnostic relevance. Disorders such as hypothyroidism, acromegaly, adrenal dysfunction and deficiencies of vitamins B12 and D produce distinct neuropathic profiles via metabolic, hormonal, inflammatory or compressive mechanisms. Subclinical nerve involvement is common, with electrophysiological abnormalities detectable in up to 60% of asymptomatic individuals. Characteristic clinical patterns - such as delayed reflexes in hypothyroidism, bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) in acromegaly and sensory ataxia in B12 deficiency - provide diagnostic clues. Based on synthesized evidence, a stepwise diagnostic algorithm was developed to guide clinical evaluation. Endocrine disorders are important and often reversible causes of peripheral neuropathy. Early recognition requires a systematic approach. The proposed evidence-based algorithm offers clinicians a practical tool to improve diagnostic efficiency, facilitate timely treatment of the underlying endocrine condition and reduce the risk of irreversible nerve damage.

candidates.title: Effects of Hydroxytyrosol at graded doses on neuroinflammation and the NF-κB pathway are associated with ameliorated cognitive decline in a rat model of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.
candidates.abstract: Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion (CCH) is a key factor in vascular cognitive impairment, and persistent neuroinflammation plays a central role in its development. Studies suggested that the Mediterranean diet, which features extra virgin olive oil (EVOO) as the primary source of fat, can significantly improve cognitive function. Hydroxytyrosol (HT), a polyphenol found in EVOO, plays a crucial role in protecting cognitive function. The present study aims to investigate the effects of HT on cognition in CCH rats and the underlying mechanisms. The rat CCH model was established by permanent bilateral common carotid artery ligation. Dl-3-n-butylphthalide (NBP) served as the positive control. HT was administered at three dose levels. Cognitive function was assessed and pathological changes in the hippocampus were examined. Levels of apoptosis, neuroinflammation, and myeloid differentiation primary response 88 (MyD88) /NF-κB pathway activity were evaluated via immunofluorescence, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and western blotting. CCH induced cognitive impairment and increased hippocampal neuronal apoptosis, as well as neuroinflammation and activation of the MyD88/NF-κB pathway in rats. These effects were partially reversed by supplementation with NBP or HT. Notably, the medium dose of HT produced the most favorable results, while the high dose did not demonstrate superior efficacy. HT treatment is associated with reduced neuroinflammation and inhibition of the MyD88/NF-κB pathway, which may contribute to the alleviation of CCH-induced cognitive impairment. The optimal effect is observed at the medium dose rather than the high dose.

candidates.title: [Preliminary investigation of the efficacy and safety of osilodostat in patients with refractory Cushing's syndrome].
candidates.abstract: Preliminary investigation on the efficacy and safety of oral osilodrostat in the treatment of patients with complicated Cushing's syndrome (CS). This study retrospectively enrolled patients with complicated CS who received osilodrostat at four hospitals from April 1, 2025 to January 31, 2026: Peking Union Medical College Hospital (17 cases), Qilu Hospital of Shandong University (1 case), Cangzhou Central Hospital (1 case), and the Second Hospital of Hebei Medical University (3 cases). Patients were followed up until March 31, 2026, to observe treatment efficacy and adverse reactions and to measure plasma osilodrostat concentrations. A total of 22 patients were enrolled, including 9 males and 13 females, with the age of [M(Q1,Q3)]61 (43, 65) years. Of these, 81.8% (18/22) had adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-dependent CS, including 8 cases of Cushing's disease and 5 cases of ectopic ACTH syndrome; 18.2% (4/22) had ACTH-independent CS. The morning serum cortisol level (8:00) in the 22 patients was 1 225.44 (847.32, 1 520.76) nmol/L. After treatment, serum cortisol decreased by approximately 40% from baseline in the 22 patients, with a treatment response rate of 72.7% (16/22). Morning serum cortisol decreased by ≥50% from baseline in 50.0% (11/22) of patients after treatment, and returned to the normal range in 40.9% (9/22). Among the 15 patients with CS in whom 24 hour urinary free cortisol (24 h UFC) was measured, the level decreased by a mean of 58% after treatment, and 73.3% (11/15) of patients had a ≥50% reduction in 24 h UFC from baseline after treatment. The median osilodrostat dose was 2.0 mg/d, and the mean osilodrostat dose in treatment responders was 2.4 mg/d. Adverse reactions of varying degrees occurred in 11 patients (50.0%, 11/22), of whom 2 (9.1%, 2/22) discontinued treatment due to adverse reactions. No serious adverse reactions were reported during follow-up. According to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE), adverse events were grade 1-3. The main adverse reactions were gastrointestinal symptoms (22.7%, 5/22) and adrenal insufficiency (13.6%, 3/22), most of which were tolerable. The trough plasma concentration of osilodrostat was 2.22(1.34,3.25) ng/ml in 6 patients. The treatment response rate of osilodrostat in Chinese patients with complicated CS was 72.7%. Adverse reactions of varying degrees occurred in 50.0% of patients, with CTCAE grades 1-3. candidates.title: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome (PSIS) is a rare congenital disorder characterized by an interrupted or absent pituitary stalk, ectopic posterior pituitary, and anterior pituitary hypoplasia, resulting in varying degrees of hypopituitarism. An 18-year-old white American male with a history of panhypopituitarism, adrenal insufficiency, and Asperger's syndrome presented with seizures. Examination revealed short stature and absent secondary sexual characteristics. Endocrine evaluation demonstrated multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a hypoplastic anterior pituitary gland, ectopic posterior pituitary, and absent pituitary stalk, confirming the diagnosis of PSIS. Hormone replacement therapy with hydrocortisone, levothyroxine, growth hormone, and testosterone enanthate was initiated. PSIS should be considered in patients with growth failure, delayed puberty, and multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies. Early recognition and timely hormone replacement are critical to optimize growth, pubertal development, and long-term outcomes.

candidates.title: Diagnostic challenge of delayed immune-related hepatitis during zongertinib treatment after nivolumab plus ipilimumab in a 52-year-old man with HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Delayed immune-related hepatitis after discontinuation of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is increasingly recognized, but attribution is difficult when liver injury develops during subsequent tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. This diagnostic dilemma has not been well described during human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-selective TKI treatment after dual ICI therapy. A 52-year-old Japanese man with HER2 exon 20 insertion-positive stage IVB non-small cell lung cancer received nivolumab plus ipilimumab from February 28 to November 13, 2025, and developed grade 2 oral mucositis, grade 2 adrenal insufficiency, and grade 1-2 skin toxicity. Zongertinib was initiated on November 26. Routine testing on January 6, 2026 showed grade 3 hepatocellular injury, and zongertinib was withheld. Despite drug withdrawal, liver injury progressed, and he was admitted with mild fatigue on January 20, when aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and γ-glutamyl transpeptidase levels were 774, 1,386, 156, and 160 U/L, respectively. Total bilirubin remained approximately 1.0 mg/dL. Viral and autoimmune testing and imaging disclosed no alternative cause. Liver biopsy showed active hepatitis with lymphocyte-predominant portal and lobular inflammation and interface activity, findings compatible with an immune-mediated hepatitis pattern but not specific for the causative agent. Prednisolone 40 mg/day (approximately 0.5 mg/kg/day) produced rapid biochemical improvement with resolution of fatigue. Zongertinib was resumed on February 11 and continued without recurrent hepatitis through June 2026. The progression of liver injury despite zongertinib withdrawal, multiple prior immune-related adverse events, exclusion of competing causes, compatible histology, corticosteroid responsiveness, and absence of recurrence after zongertinib rechallenge collectively favored delayed immune-related hepatitis, although zongertinib-associated drug-induced liver injury could not be completely excluded. In similar cases, a structured etiological assessment, including liver biopsy when the result may alter cancer treatment, can help guide management.

candidates.title: Socioeconomic Disparities in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment and Survival: Analysis of the Korean K-CURE cohort.
candidates.abstract: Breast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer worldwide and in South Korea. Although Korea provides universal health coverage, the extent to which socioeconomic status (SES) influences breast cancer care and outcomes remains unclear. This study evaluated SES-related differences in screening participation, stage at diagnosis, treatment patterns, and survival within a universal healthcare system. We analyzed 111,585 women aged ≥40 years diagnosed with breast cancer between 2014 and 2019 using the K-CURE dataset. SES was classified into five income- and insurance-based groups: Medical Benefit status and four NHI premium quartiles. Variables included screening participation, cancer stage, and treatment. Kaplan-Meier estimates compared unadjusted survival, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models estimated adjusted hazard ratios for mortality outcomes. Lower SES was associated with reduced screening participation, more advanced stage at diagnosis, and lower treatment receipt. The Medical Benefit group showed the highest proportion of distant-stage cancer (8.4%) and the highest no-treatment rate (2.7%). Mortality was substantially higher among non-screened patients across all SES groups. In multivariable analyses, low SES, advanced stage, and non-receipt of standard treatments were significant predictors of increased breast cancer-specific mortality. Despite high overall treatment rates, disparities persisted among socioeconomically disadvantaged groups. Significant income- and insurance-based socioeconomic disparities in breast cancer detection, treatment receipt, and survival remain even within a universal healthcare system. Targeted strategies to improve screening participation and ensure equitable access to care for vulnerable populations are essential to reduce SES-related survival gaps. Socioeconomic disparities persist despite universal health coverage.

candidates.title: When genetics disrupt the gut: Dysmotility and ganglioneuromatosis in multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2B syndrome.
candidates.abstract: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2B (MEN2B) is a rare hereditary cancer syndrome characterized by medullary thyroid carcinoma, mucosal neuromas, and pheochromocytoma. Gastrointestinal involvement is common and often manifests as diffuse intestinal ganglioneuromatosis (IGN), which can impair motility and lead to severe constipation, pseudo-obstruction, or megacolon. We report a male infant with known MEN2B who developed progressive abdominal distension and obstructive symptoms refractory to medical management. Initial rectal suction biopsies were unrevealing. Due to persistent symptoms, a diverting ileostomy was created for decompression, during which full-thickness biopsies were obtained, ultimately establishing the definitive diagnosis of colonic ganglioneuromatosis. This case highlights the limitations of mucosal biopsies in detecting deeper neural pathology and underscores the importance of maintaining clinical suspicion for IGN in patients with MEN2B and persistent gastrointestinal symptoms despite a normal initial evaluation.

candidates.title: Safety, recovery, and hospital resource use after robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection in a 48-hour short-stay pathway: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract: To compare perioperative safety, early recovery, and resource use between a short-stay pathway and conventional inpatient care for robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection. This single-center retrospective cohort included 110 patients who underwent robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection: 47 managed in a short-stay pathway with discharge planned within 48 h of hospital admission and 63 managed with conventional inpatient care during the same period. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of Clavien-Dindo grade II or higher complications, unplanned intensive care, emergency attendance, readmission, reoperation, or death. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative hemodynamic instability, postoperative hypotension and hypoglycemia, pain, opioid consumption, Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15), length of stay, costs, pathway completion, and patient satisfaction. Welch t tests and Fisher exact tests were used for unadjusted comparisons, and absolute risk differences (RDs) and mean differences are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Exploratory linear models with heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, ASA class, tumor size, and duration of alpha blockade; sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for surgeon, surgical approach, secretory phenotype, and hypertension. Baseline, comorbidity, endocrine, and operative characteristics were similar between groups (all standardized mean differences < 0.30). The 30-day composite safety outcome occurred in 1 of 47 short-stay patients (2.1%) and 1 of 63 conventional inpatients (1.6%; RD 0.5% points, 95% CI -6.6 to 9.6; P = 1.000). Intraoperative hemodynamic instability was also similar (83.0% vs. 87.3%; P = 0.590), as were persistent postoperative hypotension (8.5% vs. 7.9%) and postoperative hypoglycemia (8.5% vs. 7.9%). The planned 48-hour discharge target was achieved in 44 of 47 patients (93.6%). Compared with conventional care, the short-stay pathway had lower 24-hour pain scores (mean 1.8 vs. 2.4), total inpatient opioid exposure (8.7 vs. 17.7 mg morphine milligram equivalents), postoperative stay (44.2 vs. 105.1 h), total stay (49.2 vs. 476.4 h), and total in-hospital cost (CNY 49,858 vs. CNY 64,802), with higher 24-hour QoR-15 (119.7 vs. 107.9) and satisfaction (9.2 vs. 8.2); these differences remained significant after Holm correction and were consistent in fully adjusted sensitivity analyses. Among selected patients undergoing robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection, the short-stay pathway was associated with similar observed perioperative safety outcomes, faster recovery, shorter hospitalization, lower in-hospital costs, and higher patient satisfaction than conventional inpatient care. Because only two composite events occurred and the 95% CI of the risk difference was wide, these findings provide preliminary evidence of feasibility rather than proof of equivalent safety, and support prospective validation.

candidates.title: Targeting Kynurenine Synthesis Attenuated Cigarette Smoke-Induced COPD-Like Lung Injury Driven by TALDO1-Mediated Metabolic Reprogramming.
candidates.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a devastating condition characterized by airflow limitation, inflammation, and structural lung damage. Metabolic dysregulation is recognized as a critical feature, but the key metabolic drivers remain unclear. This study identifies transaldolase1 (TALDO1) as a previously unrecognized metabolic regulator in cigarette smoke (CS)-induced COPD pathogenesis. TALDO1 is markedly upregulated in airway epithelial cells by CS exposure. Elevated TALDO1 promotes mitochondrial dysfunction, whereas its genetic knockdown attenuates CS-induced lung function decline and pulmonary inflammation. Mechanistically, TALDO1 activation redirects tryptophan metabolism toward the kynurenine pathway, leading to L-kynurenine accumulation. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of this pathway significantly alleviates mitochondrial damage, while L-kynurenine supplementation exacerbates injury. Treatment with the IDO inhibitor Epacadostat ameliorates CS-induced lung impairment and inflammation in vivo. These findings define a TALDO1-kynurenine-mitochondrial injury axis linking airway epithelial metabolic reprogramming to COPD, providing translational evidence for targeting this pathway as a therapeutic strategy.

candidates.title: Diagnostic Utility and Cost Analysis of Sequential TF Immunohistochemistry in Hormone-Immunonegative Pituitary Adenomas.
candidates.abstract: To identify the routine use of all pituitary transcription factor (TF) immunohistochemistry (IHC) for pituitary adenoma diagnosis in Australia and New Zealand. To evaluate the diagnostic utility and cost analysis of selective sequential TF IHC, with SF1, followed by TPIT only if SF1-negative, and PIT1 only if SF1-and-TPIT-negative, in hormone-immunonegative pituitary adenomas. Prospective telephone survey and retrospective cohort study. The pathology laboratories of pituitary centres in Australia and New Zealand were surveyed regarding their routine use of TF IHC. At a high-volume pituitary centre in Melbourne, Australia, all three TF IHC were retrospectively applied to the latest 94 labelled null cell adenomas (NCA) diagnosed before routine TF IHC use. Diagnostic efficacy and cost analysis of the simulated selective sequential TF IHC were evaluated compared to universal TF IHC testing. A cohort of 397 hormone-immunonegative pituitary adenomas from Tübingen, Germany, served as an independent validation cohort. Only 57.1% of pituitary centres in Australia and New Zealand performed routine TF IHC. Of the 94 NCAs, TF IHC revised the diagnosis to SF1-lineage (68.1%), TPIT-lineage (18.1%), and PIT1-lineage adenomas (1.1%). There were no pituitary adenomas with multiple lineages. The simulated selective sequential TF IHC achieved >99% diagnostic accuracy in both Melbourne and Tübingen cohorts, reducing costs by 51.4% (Melbourne) and 63.6% (Tübingen) compared with universal TF IHC. Although misclassification of pituitary adenomas with multiple lineages is possible, our selective sequential TF IHC approach may offer pragmatic, economical hormone-immunonegative pituitary adenoma classification where TF IHC is not standard practice.

candidates.title: From Lethargy to Recovery: Central Diabetes Insipidus from Pituitary Metastasis in Recurrent HER2-Positive Breast Cancer Treated with Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki.
candidates.abstract: HER2-positive breast cancer is well known for its aggressive nature and high incidence of central nervous system (CNS) metastasis, often affecting the brain parenchyma or leptomeninges. However, metastasis to the pituitary gland is exceedingly rare. We report a case of ER/PR-negative, HER2-positive breast cancer recurrence presenting with panhypopituitarism (PH) and central diabetes insipidus (CDI), resulting in hypernatremia-induced altered mental status. The patient had completed prior treatment with neoadjuvant chemotherapy, lumpectomy, and trastuzumab. Imaging revealed a temporal lobe mass with suprasellar enhancement. Surgical resection confirmed breast carcinoma metastasis. Hormonal studies confirmed PH and CDI. Management involved DDAVP, corticosteroids, fluid correction, whole-brain radiation, and systemic therapy with fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki (ENHERTU), leading to significant neurological recovery. This case highlights a rare metastatic pattern and the need for high clinical suspicion and multidisciplinary intervention.
